corrections: The registered G-B2 bar (relative to $\lVert u_{\rm all}-u_\varnothing\rVert$) was too tight for a 32-term Möbius sum; it was restated relative to the largest corner norm (A6), found on the smoke.
Offline reference identity compares case descriptors, not the cohort hash, because the last bit of `np.exp` differs across NumPy versions (A6).
The first resource certificates under-priced the reference retry path and the pseudo-spectral cross-check; they were repriced before submission (A7, job audits refs2d-1..3).

E0's tight re-solve of a refined triple at the round-off floor was far more expensive per level than the production solve (per-level timings in DESIGN A9); `ref2b` and `ref2c` were cancelled, their completed cases kept, and the reruns (`ref2r`, `ref3b`) skip that re-solve: such cases are terminal 'unresolved-floor' and non-rankable (A9).

The first A9 eligibility rule was per window only, so an A9-terminal case with an accepted W2 window would have been rankable; fixed so every window of such a case is ineligible (A9.1, audit codex-job-a9-1).

Job reservations were priced at the certificate time limits, which proved conservative; the table 'Certificates against elapsed time' compares each certificate's projection with the Slurm elapsed time.
At $T=1.0$ the first eligibility code let a failed whole-case reference keep an accepted window and took W2 eligibility from the wrong horizon; fixed before submission (A11.1, audit codex-job-t1-1).
G-R2 on 3D val64 case 43 failed only because E0's own saved IC array differs in the last bit from the initial rows of E0's own levels; the shared-IC requirement was restated level-wise (A13).

At $T=1.0$, E0's tight re-solve of a failing base triple was far more expensive per level than the production solve (per-level timings in DESIGN A14); `ref2t1` was cancelled after dev6 case 5 and the val32 cases rerun without that retry (`ref2t1w`): such cases are terminal and non-rankable (A14). Of the two measured retries, dev6 1 stayed unresolved and dev6 5 was certified (A14.1).

A14.1 suggested the A14 rule might have cost rankable cases; it did not: a case certified by the tight retry has no production-tolerance level to match E0 or the $T=0.5$ reference, so it is non-rankable under the registered G-R2 / prefix rules anyway (A14.2). The A14 / A14.1 times quoted as case durations were cumulative log timestamps (A14.3).

Two analysis caches were defeated by eager `dict.setdefault` arguments (a QR per case; performance only, identical values). The first local B7/B8 analyses were terminated without output on the shared machine (no OOM record; high load) and rerun one at a time (A12.2).
jcp-qualify's raw archives were moved to the cluster during the analysis (COMMON-BRIEF 16); G-B3 / G-L1 read hash-verified cached copies (A12).

The results audit found that the dominance rule compared the largest candidate only with the second largest; it now compares with every resolved candidate (two counts changed, no label; A14.3, audit codex-results-1).
